engine_name: Heart-Rate Training Zones: Tanaka 2001 age-predicted maximum heart rate (HRmax = 208 − 0.7 × age, or a measured HRmax 100–220 entered by the member), zones by heart-rate reserve (Karvonen) when resting heart rate is given and by % HRmax otherwise, ACSM 11th ed. table 5.2 fractions (Easy 30–39 % HRR / 57–63 % HRmax; Moderate 40–59 % / 64–76 %; Hard 60–89 % / 77–95 %), every bound rounded to whole bpm half-up (D3-31)
intended_use: Shows three heart-rate ranges in bpm (Easy, Moderate, Hard) with the talk-test line for each and the estimated maximum, as a guide for the workout plans (FR3-11). The talk test is the final guide.
eligibility: Adults aged 18 to 99; resting heart rate optional (30–120); measured HRmax optional (100–220, must exceed resting heart rate by at least 30). No zones for heart-rate-lowering medicine Yes or Not sure (FR3-53 AS-02), a declared heart condition or pregnancy; under 18 stops. Over 75 with no exercise history sees the safety-matrix 'check with your doctor before starting intense exercise' note.
sources: Tanaka H, Monahan KD, Seals DR. Age-predicted maximal heart rate revisited. J Am Coll Cardiol 2001;37:153–6 (HRmax = 208 − 0.7 × age; meta-analysis of 351 studies).
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (2021), chapter 5, table 5.2 (intensity classification by % HRR and % HRmax).
Karvonen MJ, et al. Ann Med Exp Biol Fenn 1957;35:307–15 (heart-rate reserve method).
limitations: Formulas like this can be 10 to 12 beats out for an individual; the talk test is the final guide.
Zones do not apply with beta-blockers or other heart-rate-lowering medicines, with a declared heart condition, or in pregnancy.
Self-reported resting heart rate and measured maximum.
regulatory_statement: Approved by the owner as clinical reviewer on 3 November 2026 (P3-5A sign-off record, NFR3-14). General information, not a diagnosis, not a medical device.
licence: Lifeline Daily's own implementation of published formulas and ACSM intensity bands; free to use.
